text:
sam: Heads up — during today's noon batching window in us-west-2 we're seeing transient east-west p95 jump from ~2ms to ~30-40ms between GPU nodes in rack-3. Started ~12:03, lasted ~40s. No dropped pods but batch tail latency spiked.

deeppa: saw it on logs too, correlates with a big burst of long sequences hitting the GPU pool. Any packet loss counters?

alex: i pulled sflow/traces from the ToR and noticed TX-QLEN spikes and a burst on the tx ring for ena0 on node-gpu-07. Not classic MTU mismatch.

infra-bot: [alert] high-eastwest-latency us-west-2/rack-3 detected at 2025-11-12T19:03:12Z. affected_nodes: node-gpu-05..node-gpu-10.

jia: ran `ethtool -S ena0` on node-gpu-07, snippet below:
```
tx_packets: 12563412
rx_packets: 12563099
tx_dropped: 0
rx_missed: 0
tx_restart_queue: 87
tx_busy: 1200
```
seems like tx_restart_queue and tx_busy correlate with spike windows.

sam: interesting. Could be NIC driver backpressure or eswitch QoS mishandling during big continuous batching flows. Any RDMA offload in this cluster?

alex: no RDMA on these SKUs — soft-queue growth + offload toggle difference between kernel versions (5.10 vs 5.15) observed. node-gpu-08 was on 5.15 after a maintenance deploy earlier today.

deeppa: so hypothesis: kernel/driver change + bursty long-token requests cause tx queue saturation which increases serialization and east-west latency. Quick mitigation: pin large-batch workloads to other racks, and rollback kernel on node-gpu-08 for canary check?

ops-oncall: I've drained node-gpu-08 and cordoned it, bumped scheduler to avoid rack-3 for large sequence profiles. Will monitor next window. :white_check_mark:

jia: also adding a short-term tc qdisc rule to limit per-flow bursts on the ToR egress for affected nodes, should smooth queues: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000` — applying now.

alex: good. let's also capture `tcp_info` and fq stats during the next window and open a kernel bug if we repro. Who wants ownership to follow up on vendor driver with packet captures?

sam: alex take vendor driver + packet captures. deepa will own scheduling changes + rollout blocker if rollback is needed. ops-oncall will watch monitoring and rollback drain. I'll add a short incident blurb in the morning.

infra-bot: incident-note created: IN-20251112-3 — transient e2w tx-queue saturation in rack-3 during batch window.

deeppa: thanks. once we confirm the kernel/driver diff repro, we'll schedule a larger postmortem and check autoscaler policies so big batches don't concentrate in one rack.

alex: quick log command if anyone needs it: `sudo cat /sys/class/net/ena0/queues/tx-*/xmit_more` and `sudo ethtool -S ena0 | grep tx_restart_queue`

sam: short update expected in ~30m, will ping thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
